title: gridui-07: Crate-review debt
summary: Debito tecnico del crate: docs, allocazioni, test coverage, helper condivisi.
description:
Debt found by reviewing the crate rather than by a user hitting it: values the vocabulary could not express, and rules a caller had to remember.

⭐ READ docs/layout.md BEFORE TOUCHING ANY TASK IN THIS PHASE. The authoring API changed under these tasks on 2026-09-16 and several of them are written against the older one.

═══════════ WHAT THE LAYOUT API IS NOW (2026-09-16) ═══════════
Uncommitted on feat/hint-collapses-to-the-tree. Every spelling below goes through ONE parser shared with the wire, so the line written in Rust is the line a plugin writes in JSON.

1. EVERY VALUE READS ITS CSS SPELLING. `Track` ("auto", "1fr", "200px", "22", "min-content", "repeat(3, 1fr)"), and the layout keywords `Justify` / `Align` / `Direction` ("space-between", "center", "column") through their own serde names, hyphen and underscore alike. Eight builders take `impl Into<..>`; ~100 hand-written enum variants were swept out of real code, and six imports went dead as a result. The track parser used to live in heca-view-realize, which meant a plugin could say "1fr" and native Rust could not.

2. THE GRID IS CSS-SHAPED. `.template_row(..)` / `.template_column(..)` / `.template_area(..)` on the container; `.child(one_or_many)` auto-places, exactly as in HTML. PLACEMENT IS THE CHILD'S OWN PROPERTY — `.column("1 / -1")`, `.row(2)`, `.column_span(Span::All)`, `.area("title")` — and `.cell(child, col, row, col_span, row_span)` and `.row(child)` are GONE from the grid: a parent writing a position into its child was the inversion this replaced. Names and `1 / -1` are resolved during LAYOUT, against whichever grid holds the child, so a child can be built before its parent and a template change re-places children without rebuilding them. The described path matches: `realize` sets `area` / `col` / `row` on the child.

3. ONE DOOR FOR CHILDREN. `.child(x)` and `.child([a, b, c])` are the same builder, on every widget and on the SDK's `ViewNode`. The `child` / `children` pair is deleted.

4. `flex-basis` EXISTS — `.basis(..)`. A share is `.grow(w).basis(0.0).shrink(1.0)`, real CSS `flex: 1 1 0`. This is P052(F004)/T350 item 1, landed; see that task for what remains of it.

5. `Icon` and `NfIcon` implement `LayoutExt`, because a widget that cannot place itself cannot be a grid item. `CardGrid`, `Visibility` and `KeyHintGroup` still implement no builder trait — untouched, and worth a look.

═══════════ TWO DEFECTS FIXED THE SAME DAY ═══════════
- A row baseline-aligned children that were whole LAYOUTS, not text runs. `Flex::on_layout` hunts for the text inside each child so a name and a dimmed suffix share a line; hunting through any container made the exposé's strip treat each column of pane cards as a word, and a column of two panes was pushed down by half a card and drawn past the bottom of the map. It now looks only through TRANSPARENT wrappers — `Base::transparent`, the same answer the picker uses to the same question. The map's own overflow guard could not catch it because every fixture gave each column exactly one pane; the fixture takes pane counts per column now.
- Mouse hit-testing hand-rolled the pane area four times, with a dead 40px strip on the left (a deleted rail's width) and the right edge guarded by an x compared against half the window's HEIGHT. It asks `content_rect` and `Rectangle::contains` now.

═══════════ HOW THE WORK IS EXPECTED TO GO ═══════════
Every capability above landed with a guard that was run RED against its own bug by sabotage. Two of them passed first and proved nothing — one because the retired wire name still worked, one because `grow` alone divides free space correctly in a simple box — and were rewritten until a sabotage turned them red. A green test here is not evidence; a watched-red one is.

tasks.title: gridui-debt Dialog font-derived min-width needs Style min_width
tasks.description:
**Rescued from the old root `HANDOFF.md` §3c (deleted 2026-07-13); do not lose this.**

A short confirm dialog ("Delete Pane?") renders **cramped** — the panel hugs its content, so a two-word title + two buttons produces a tiny box, and dialogs of different content have visibly different widths with no shared baseline.

## The gap
`Style` (`heca-grid-ui/src/style.rs`) has **no `min_width`** — only `width`/`height` (`Length::{Auto, Px}`). So `Dialog` cannot express "hug the content, but never below a sensible floor".

## Work
1. Add `min_width: Length` (and probably `min_height` for symmetry — decide) to `Style`, defaulting to `Length::Auto`, and wire it into `Style::to_taffy()` (taffy has `min_size`). Add the builder to `LayoutExt`.
2. Give `Dialog`'s panel a **font-derived** minimum — the note said **~22em** (i.e. `22 × base font`), so it scales with the theme font instead of being a magic pixel count. Verify against the real dialogs (delete-pane confirm, the rename form).
3. Tests: a `min_width` smaller than the content is a no-op; larger than the content floors the box; it scales with the base font.
4. `docs/widgets.md`: the `Style`/`LayoutExt` tables + the `Dialog` entry.

## Why it's here
`gridui-07` (crate-review debt) is the right home: it is a missing primitive in the layout style, not a feature.

## Gates
clippy 0; `cargo test -p heca-grid-ui -p heca`; showcase green; no `cargo fmt`.

tasks.title: A proportional share must not be written as a fixed measure
tasks.description:
# The problem

To make two containers take half a region each, `with_share` (`heca/src/chrome/mod.rs`) writes:

```rust
layout.flex_grow = grow;
layout.height = heca_grid_ui::Length::Px(0.0);      // ← a FIXED measure
layout.min_height = Some(heca_grid_ui::Length::Px(0.0));
layout.flex_shrink = Some(1.0);
```

**A proportional share is being expressed by writing a fixed number**, which is what the user does not
want anyone doing (2026-07-28: *"I don't want other developers to write fixed measure"*). Worse, it is
three coupled fields whose combination is folklore: get one wrong and the split silently reverts to
content-sizing, which is exactly the bug it was written to fix.

# Why it is there

`flex_grow` distributes only **positive free space**. Container content is routinely taller than a
sidebar, so there is no positive free space to distribute — measured 2026-07-28: two containers took
**1214px each inside a 600px body** and divided nothing. In CSS the answer is `flex: 1 1 0`; the base
size of 0 is what makes the whole region free space. With it: **296px each**, measured.

**`Layout` has no `flex_basis`** (confirmed — `grep flex_basis heca-grid-ui/src/style.rs` is empty),
so `height = Px(0)` is standing in for it. taffy *does* have `flex_basis` in its `Style`, so the
concept is available one layer down and simply was never surfaced.

# What to build

1. **Add `flex_basis: Option<Length>` to `Layout`** and map it in `to_taffy`
   (`heca-grid-ui/src/style.rs`). That is the missing word in the vocabulary; everything below already
   understands it.
2. **Give the library one way to say "take a share"** so no caller assembles the trio by hand — a
   builder on `LayoutExt` (`heca-grid-ui/src/builders.rs`), e.g. `share(n)`, meaning *n shares of the
   parent's main axis*, setting grow + basis 0 + min 0 + shrink internally. Then:
   - `with_share` becomes one call and stops naming a measure;
   - the SDK's `Style` trait (`heca-view/src/build.rs`) exposes the same thing, so a **described** tree
     can say it too — today it can only set `flex_grow`, which has the same trap;
   - `grow()` stays as the raw flex knob for callers who genuinely want content-based basis.
   Decide whether `grow()` should be *renamed* or documented as the low-level one, so the obvious name
   is the one that behaves as expected.
3. **Main-axis, not height.** `flex_basis` is main-axis relative like `flex_grow`, so one setter covers
   a column and a row (the same reason `ContainerContribution::grow` is not called `height_grow`). Do
   not add a per-axis variant.
4. **Sweep for the same folklore elsewhere.** `ScrollRegion::new()` already sets `min_height: 0` and
   `flex_shrink: 1` by hand with a long comment explaining why (`heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/scroll_region.rs:274`).
   Check whether that is the same idea written a second way, and whether it should go through the new
   setter.
5. **Tests must measure, not inspect flags.** A test asserting `flex_grow == 1.0` passed while the
   layout was visibly broken (2026-07-28) — the measured-height test is what caught it. Assert
   pixels: two shares of a 600px region are ~296 each, with content far taller than either.

# Acceptance

- No caller writes a fixed measure to express a proportion — not in `heca`, not in the SDK, not in a
  described tree.
- One setter, documented, with the trio behind it.
- `docs/widgets.md` says how to take a share, next to R8 (the stretch contract) in
  `docs/chrome-and-ui.md` — the two rules are read together.
- Whole workspace green, clippy 0 warnings.
tasks.notes:
PARTLY LANDED 2026-09-16, uncommitted on feat/hint-collapses-to-the-tree.

THIS TASK PREDICTED A REAL DEFECT AND IT HAPPENED. The "three coupled fields whose combination is folklore" (flex_grow + height: Px(0) + min_height + flex_shrink) were still being written by hand in the exposé's share_v, and the zero HEIGHT half of it was the wrong spelling: a definite zero height says "this box is zero", which is a different answer to anything measuring the container's content than "start from nothing, then take your weight".

WHAT LANDED
- heca-grid-ui gained the property that was missing: LayoutExt::basis(..) → Style::Layout::flex_basis → taffy flex_basis. CSS flex-basis, taking pixels, a percentage or "auto". It is a Layout field, so it travels on the wire with no name table to extend.
- A share is now written .grow(w).basis(0.0).shrink(1.0) — literally CSS `flex: 1 1 0`. heca/src/chrome/expose/mod.rs::share_v uses it, and the comment that apologised for spelling it with a zero height is gone.
- Guard: a_share_divides_the_whole_box_by_weight_not_just_the_leftover (heca-grid-ui/src/builders.rs). It took two attempts — the first passed with the mapping deleted and therefore proved nothing, because grow alone divides free space correctly in a simple box. The rewritten one gives the two items DIFFERENT CONTENT, which is where the basis bites: asked for 2:1 in a 900px box, a zero basis gives 600/300 and an auto basis gives 606/294, skewed by what each item started from. Sabotaged, it fails on exactly that.

WHAT IS LEFT, and it is the original scope
- `with_share` in heca/src/chrome/mod.rs still writes the four fields by hand. It is the function this task was opened about; share_v was its twin in the exposé. It should call .basis(0.0) too, or better, be deleted in favour of one shared builder.
- The larger question this task asks — "a proportional share must not be written as a fixed measure" — is answerable now that basis exists. A share is three builders; consider whether it should be ONE (`.share(w)`), so the combination stops being folklore a caller has to remember at all.

RELATED, same day: docs/layout.md now documents the share idiom, each of the three parts, and what each alone does instead.

tasks.title: A widget invents a slot instead of taking a template — and then finds the part by its position
tasks.description:
Filed 2026-09-16, scope decided with Antonio 2026-09-17.

THE DECISION
**A widget does not invent slots. It holds one child, and that child is a `Grid` saying the arrangement.**

`DockFrame::header(..)` and the pane's header slot answer exactly one shape. Header | Content | Footer needs a second slot; a fourth part needs a third. `.template_row("auto 1fr auto")` answers all of them in one line a reader can check against the picture — and it is the same line for a dock, a pane, a palette or a plugin's panel.

So `Pane` and `DockFrame` stay **frames**: border, glow, fold, title chrome. The arrangement is a `Grid` child.

THE DEFECT THIS REMOVES
A widget with several PARTS finds each part by its index in `base.children`. `children[0]` is the header, `children[1]` the body, `children.len() == 2` means "there is a header". Put a second thing in the body and the first is mistaken for a header; insert a part and every index after it is wrong; and no test fails, because the indices are still valid indices. `dock_frame.rs` documents it as the design: "Index of the header (a `Flex` row) / body within `base.children`."

The slot is the cause and the index is the symptom: a part placed by a named area or a template row is found by name, and the question never arises.

THE SURVEY — non-test code finding a part by child position (measured 2026-09-16):
- heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/dialog.rs — 17 (`self.base.children[0]` at :240, :277, :296-297)
- heca/src/chrome/mod.rs — 11
- heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/scroll_region.rs — 10
- heca/src/chrome/overlay.rs — 3; heca/src/chrome/expose/pane_card.rs — 3
- heca/src/chrome/scene.rs — 2; heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/flex.rs — 2
- one each: heca/src/chrome/pane/mod.rs, heca/src/providers/workspaces/pane_row.rs, heca/src/components/folder_line.rs, heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/tag.rs, heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/visibility.rs
- heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/dock_frame.rs — header/body/rail indices, named in its own module doc

WHAT EXISTS NOW (landed 2026-09-16, commit 47356a0)
`.template_row(..)` / `.template_column(..)` / `.template_area(..)` on the container; `.child(one_or_many)` auto-places as in HTML; placement is the CHILD's property — `.area("header")`, `.column("1 / -1")`, `.row(2)`, `.column_span(Span::All)` — resolved during layout against whichever grid holds the child. Full reference: docs/layout.md.

THE WORK
1. **`Pane`** — delete its header slot; the caller passes a `Grid`. `heca/src/chrome/pane/shell.rs` builds `Grid::new().template_row("auto 1fr").child([header, content])` (or `"auto 1fr auto"` when something wants a footer), and `heca/src/chrome/pane/mod.rs::header_height` asks for the named area instead of `match children.len()`.
2. **`DockFrame`** — same: delete `header(..)`, keep the frame's own chrome (fold toggle, rail, brackets). Its header/body/rail indices go with it.
3. **`Dialog`** — 17 positional lookups; title / body / actions as a template.
4. Then the app-side ones, and `scroll_region` LAST — it is 2565 lines with its own split task (P082(F003)/T471, deferred); change only how it finds its parts, or agree the order first.

EDGE CASES
- `flex.rs`'s two are inside `on_layout`'s baseline pass — a walk over all children, not a part lookup. Check before changing.
- `visibility.rs` and `tag.rs` may genuinely mean "the one child". A wrapper with exactly one child is not this defect; leave a comment saying why when it stays.
- Deleting a slot builder is an API change for that widget's callers, including the described path — `realize` reads `slot` props (`header`, `leading`, `trailing`). Decide per widget whether `slot` maps to a grid area or is dropped, and keep the described and native paths saying the same thing.
- `Item`'s leading/trailing are a genuinely different case: they are a row of three parts with fixed meaning, not an arrangement a caller chooses. Judge it separately rather than sweeping it.

VERIFICATION
Per widget: a guard that puts a SECOND thing in the body and asserts the first is still not mistaken for the header — the failure an index cannot see. Sabotage each one. Then Antonio drives what changed: a dock's header and fold, a pane's info bar, a confirm dialog, a scrolled list.

NOT IN SCOPE: the general "the app uses Flex everywhere and Grid nowhere" backlog (`Grid::new()` appears zero times in heca/src). Bigger conversation, its own proposal.

⚠️ Antonio, 2026-09-17: most phases in this feature are likely obsolete or superseded and want reviewing. This task is filed here for now, not because F004's phase structure is right.
